title: Embroidery (machine, job-work)
subtitle: Computerised multi-head embroidery on fabric for sarees, dress material and garments
covers: This page covers machine embroidery units. Most do job-work for traders, charged per 1,000 stitches. Hand embroidery and zari thread making are not covered here (zari has its own page).

snapshot.text: Surat is estimated to have about 40,000 embroidery units (TOI, Sep 2026) and about 1.5 lakh embroidery machines (2026 SITEX profile).
Embroidery thread got costlier in 2026: viscose embroidery yarn up about 12% in four months, polyester and spun embroidery yarn up to 35%.
A 2026 labour dispute over weekly offs led to machines standing idle in some units; most workers are migrants from Bihar, UP and Jharkhand.

items.text: An embroidery unit runs computerised multi-head machines that stitch designs onto processed fabric or garment panels, often adding sequins and cords.
Units are spread across Katargam, Varachha, Pandesara and other areas.

steps.d: Design is digitised into a machine file and a sample is run.
Trader's fabric is framed on the multi-head machine.
All heads stitch the same design; sequins or cords are added where ordered.
Pieces checked, counted and returned with the job-work bill.

blocks.note: Public quotes only, with date and source. Trade-site quotes are indicative; a customer's own purchase bills always win. Trend arrows only where the source itself gives a direction.

items.text: Absolute rupee prices for embroidery thread were not found in public sources; collect the customer's purchase bills.
GST on man-made fibre was cut from 18% to 5% and on man-made yarn from 12% to 5% (GST Council, 3 Sep 2025).
CPCB's White list includes hand embroidery and zari work units; machine embroidery was not found by name in the lists checked, so its category is Unknown.
GPCB's June 2025 order exempts White-category units from Consent to Establish and Consent to Operate, but they must inform GPCB and self-declare compliance.
Ask for the GPCB intimation or consent and the factory licence status.
Workers reported 12-hour shifts with no paid weekly off; after a 2026 dispute the units' association announced 8-hour shifts at minimum wage. Some units had machines idle as workers left.
Labour is largely migrant. About 30% of migrant workers reportedly did not return after the 2024 election and wedding season, and some units stopped night shifts.
Make, age and price of multi-head machines: collect invoices and valuation.

Power: GERC's FY2025-26 DGVCL tariff schedule lists the Non-RGP rate (loads up to 40 kW) at 435 paise a unit up to 10 kW and 465 paise above 10 kW, plus fixed charges and 45 paise extra in peak hours. Larger loads fall in other categories. A new FY2026-27 order was issued on 25 Mar 2026, so confirm current rates from the customer's bills.

Payment terms from traders and bad-debt history: no public figure. Read from the customer's ledger.

cells: About Rs 0.20-0.50 per 1,000 stitches (trade-site FAQ, unverified)

items.text: Embroidery is 'Activity 2' under Gujarat Textile Policy 2024 (capital subsidy 20% / 18% / 10% by taluka category, interest subsidy, power subsidy).

sections.title: Fragility points and early warning signs for a lender

items.text: Thread cost spikes that units can pass on only partly.
Labour disputes and migrant workers leaving.
Fashion risk: demand depends on traders' saree and dress orders; when traders hold old stock, embroidery orders dry up first.
Cheque returns or frequent overdraws; cash credit used near the limit all month.
Electricity units falling month on month, or a shift stopped, without a matching fall in loan outstanding.
Creditor days stretching; suppliers charging late-payment interest; purchases switched to cash from new sources.
Stock or receivables building up; sales concentrated on one or two parties or brokers.
Wages paid late or labour leaving; regular weekly closures.
New borrowing from private lenders or related parties; machines rented out or sold.
